notes:
Summary: StratoQuill builds a latency-first reranking layer for programmatic ad auctions. Very cost-sensitive due to CPM margins. Talking to Priya + Jordan.

Key things they care about: p95 latency for rerank < 50ms, throughput 200-400 QPS (peak), cost per 1M tokens must be below their current self-hosted baseline. Interested in batching but only if p95 stays <50ms, heavy interest in prefix/KV cache to cut token compute, and aggressive quantization (4-bit / int4) to reduce GPU footprint.

Security: EU customer data must stay in EU region, need SSO + audit logs + KMS integration. They asked for an exported audit-log format example.

Commercial: mid-market ARR target for Redwood Dedicated; initial POC to validate perf and unit economics then expand to reserved capacity.

Shorthand from last call: "If we can hit 45ms p95 with 4-bit quant + cache at 60% cost reduction, we move fast." — CTO (L. Moretti).

Notes on engagement: AE Jordan doing pricing; SE Priya owns benchmark runs; legal loop for data residency. Action owners added in Drive doc.

requirements_summary: Workload: reranking for programmatic auction (short-context, ~80-150 tokens per request). Targets: p95 latency <= 50ms (goal 40-45ms), sustained throughput 200-400 req/s, burst to 1k req/s for 30s. Cost sensitivity: want >=50% reduction vs current self-hosted fp16 GPU cluster. Must support EU data residency and SSO. Prefer open models compatible with quantization (LLaMA/psi variants). Require routing/fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained.
poc_plan: Week 1: baseline fp16 runs (small model family) - measure p50/p95, token cost
Week 2: Apply 4-bit quantized model variants + kernel tuning; run batching matrix (no-batch, micro-batch 4, micro-batch 8) and measure latency tail
Week 3: Enable KV/prefix cache; measure hit rate and effective token reduction; test cold vs warm cache scenarios
Deliverable: comparative perf report (latency/cost/throughput) and recommended config for Redwood Dedicated
